content:
I made this PR Physlib#1797 which will add to each PR made after it a summary of the declarations added, and the files changed in a given PR. This will hopefully help reviews.

This is based on what Mathlib already has. It is not perfect, but am working under the principle of something here is better than nothing. If anyone has suggestions of what we can add to the summary in the future, it would be great to hear them.
Will test this out tomorrow!

I'm not actually sure the best way to test things like this locally. There you can generate the message locally, and there are some guides on how to do that in the description. If you have a better solution, I would love to hear it
Do you mean testing the GitHub action part of your PR? If so after some surfing I have seen this community tool called act which allows you to test this locally
Yes - but with the addition of seeing how it actually acts on a new PR as well.
Mhm I'm not sure if act can help with comment path, it might be better to try and run this on another test repo. Could we merge this into a test branch on physlib and check it on a PR?
Example here: https://github.com/jstoobysmith/JTSphyslib/pull/3

Okay this looks good, though I'm wondering does this need to be automatic for every new PR to physlib, maybe we only need the manual element when a reviewer wants to see this. Thinking about it from a personal workflow, for small to medium PRs I usually go straight to the diff, but for large PRs it's definitely helpful to have this

The workflow runs anyway to add the PR message which is currently being put on the project. It now takes a bit longer 1m 42s, but I'm not sure this is too bad. We could make a command /summary which when commented puts this summary on, if this is what you would think is better.
Mhm in that case might as well do this summary along with that; would this update if we give review comments and there are more commits?
Ah good point - no it wouldn't. I don't think this would be too hard to fix though.
Okk and maybe as a follow up we can figure out how to pick up split line declarations

Yeah - I think I know the solution to this: Mathlib has a lean aware diff, whilst the one I implemented above (with AIs help) was a text-based diff. Seeing how easy it is to adapt Mathlib's lean aware diff.

Alas, I don't know how to do the lean aware diff without first building the project. I've updated this PR though so that the summary will now update on commits.

The script here is AI written, and I see AI as a really useful tool at allowing us to build scripts like this which help us with the project. Im wondering though if there is a way to be more systematic and controlled in their writing. Maybe the benefit here outweighs the risk, but I think in general it is something we should consider.
Might be a bit naive but to start we could put a tag on vibecoded scripts so we can keep track
When I vibe-lean locally, I usually tag the proofs or sections that are AI generated as I often lose track otherwise
The tagging is quite simple I just use capitalized docstring

I don't think this is naive at all - just realized that this is essentially what we have done with Physlib and PhyslibAlpha - should we have ./scripts and ./scripts/Alpha with the same review principles?
Yess I think this is good, and then can "promote" scripts from alpha to the main directory with higher review standards
I took a look and it seems reasonable to me but I'm not particularly knowledgeable on this stuff

I did the following:

  1. Moved the script from ./scripts/github to ./scripts/alpha/github
  2. Changed the output so it more closely matches that of: https://github.com/alexjbest/leaff. An example is https://github.com/jstoobysmith/JTSphyslib/pull/4 (there are two output messages their, the second one is the one of relevance).
  3. Asked Fable 5.1. to clean up the script so it is easier to understand (with limited success).

I think Physlib#1797 is ready for review.

This looks like it is working ok.

One other feature that it might be worth adding, is suggesting reviewers to PRs based on previous PRs.
Yes I think this would be great, is it previous PRs reviewed or PRs submitted and merged? I think it would be great to have both
I think ideally PRs submitted and merged would be the best metric here, as it will also get those who have never reviewed before involved (hopefully)

I think this metric suggested above is best, as I think alot of contributors are not directly active on zulip. I also think with regards to the PR reviews, maybe it would be worth updating the readme of the project?

Currently it does not really mention reviews as a way of contributing and also implies that maintainers are the only one's who can review. We could maybe say that anyone can review PRs and the final verdict/merge rights are with maintainers
